dialogue_summary: The user and AI are collaborating to plan a design system audit and establish a strategy for migrating live website pages into editable Figma components. The AI has provided the user with a detailed AntiGravity brief and testing checklist to initiate the codebase scan for design drift.

step_1_outcomes.text: Design system audit and Figma migration plan (Phase 9)
Design system audit workflow and scope definition
AntiGravity design audit brief and testing checklist

step_1_intentions.intention: Design system auditing and workflow definition

step_2_requirements.text: The project deliverable must focus on research and planning rather than execution.
step_2_requirements.rationale: The AI explicitly defines the scope of the request as a research and planning task rather than an execution task.

step_2_requirements.text: The project must be structured and designated as 'Phase 9 — Design System Formalization + Figma Migration'.
step_2_requirements.rationale: The AI explicitly defines the project as a new phase with this specific designation.

step_2_requirements.text: The migration strategy must define a method to convert website pages into editable, workable Figma components.
step_2_requirements.rationale: The user explicitly requests to bring website pages into Figma as editable, workable components.

step_2_requirements.text: The deliverable must include research identifying the tools to use, the steps to execute, and instructions for the migration and audit process.
step_2_requirements.rationale: The user explicitly asks for research on tools, steps, and instructions for the migration and audit process.

step_2_requirements.text: The technical feasibility assessment must account for the constraint that WebGL/canvas elements (such as shaders, box animations, Vanta NET, dot/graph grids, GSAP) cannot be captured or imported as live editable elements into Figma.
step_2_requirements.rationale: The AI identifies a hard technical constraint that WebGL/canvas elements cannot be imported into Figma, which must be factored into the feasibility assessment.

step_2_requirements.text: The current design system and its current state must be identified and audited.
step_2_requirements.rationale: The user explicitly requests to understand the current design system and its current state.

step_2_requirements.text: The design system audit must analyze the existing project files, specifically 'design-system-source.md', 'colors_and_type.css', and 'CANONICAL_SPEC.md'.
step_2_requirements.rationale: The AI identifies these specific existing project files as the source material that must be examined to understand the current design system.

step_2_requirements.text: The delivery workflow must require the AI to wait for the user to input 'start task' after the preamble before delivering the first complete step.
step_2_requirements.rationale: The AI explicitly clarifies the sequencing constraint that it must wait for 'start task' before delivering the next step.

step_2_requirements.text: The first step delivered after the 'start task' trigger must include the full AntiGravity brief and a testing checklist.
step_2_requirements.rationale: The AI explicitly states that replying 'start task' will result in the delivery of the full AntiGravity brief and testing checklist.

step_2_requirements.text: The design system audit must be conducted as a phased, audit-first workflow before any Figma migration.
step_2_requirements.rationale: The user asks if the audit should be done before Figma migration, and the AI establishes a phased, audit-first workflow as the architected path forward.

step_2_requirements.text: AntiGravity must scan the codebase and produce a drift inventory.
step_2_requirements.rationale: The AI explicitly plans for AntiGravity to scan the codebase and produce a drift inventory as part of the audit setup.

step_2_requirements.text: The repository must be confirmed as open and ready for AntiGravity to scan before starting the code extraction.
step_2_requirements.rationale: The AI states a mandatory prerequisite that it needs to confirm the repository is open and ready to scan before kicking off the extraction.

step_2_requirements.text: The design audit must be read-only and must not modify any source files.
step_2_requirements.rationale: The audit brief explicitly mandates that the process is read-only and no source files are to be modified.

step_2_requirements.text: The audit must produce exactly one report file named 'design-audit-raw.md' located at the repository root.
step_2_requirements.rationale: The brief requires producing one report file, and the testing checklist specifies it must be named 'design-audit-raw.md' and exist at the repository root.

step_2_slots.text: Decision on which migration route to proceed with (Plugin vs. MCP).
The decision on how to proceed with or modify the design system after the audit is complete.
Inclusion of YouTube videos, instructions, or specific internet resources related to the learning topics.
Decision on what the editable Figma source of truth should be built from.
Confirmation of the audit scope (whether to audit all shipped pages or just completed ones).
Confirmation of the canonical reference source and drift definition (treating colors_and_type.css as canonical).
Confirmation of the drift categorization buckets (exact match, near-miss, and orphan).

step_3_all_actions.text: User asks to convert website pages into editable Figma components.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: I want to flesh out all the pages and then, you know, bring them into Figma as editable, workable components

step_3_all_actions.text: User asks to identify and audit the current design system.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: I want to also understand what is the current design system and what is the current state of this and then later I will decide what to do with it.

step_3_all_actions.text: User asks for research on tools, steps, and instructions for the migration and audit process.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: do the research and give me what is the tools to use and how to do it and the steps to do it

step_3_all_actions.text: User asks for relevant YouTube videos or internet resources.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: I find like if there is any YouTube videos or instructions or specific things in the internet available related to all these things

step_3_all_actions.text: AI analyzes the user's request as a research and planning task.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: This is a research and planning request rather than an execution task

step_3_all_actions.text: AI evaluates the technical feasibility of converting live sites to Figma using plugins and MCP.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: I need to verify the technical feasibility: can I actually convert a live website into editable Figma components?

step_3_all_actions.text: AI examines the user's existing project files to understand the current design system.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: I should be reading through his existing project files—the design-system-source.md, colors_and_type.css, CANONICAL_SPEC.md

step_3_all_actions.text: AI defines the project as a new phase for design system formalization and migration.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: New phase, call it Phase 9 — Design System Formalization + Figma Migration.

step_3_all_actions.text: AI identifies the core technical constraint regarding WebGL/canvas elements.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: Your site is heavily WebGL — chrome head shader, box animation, Vanta NET, dot/graph grids, GSAP. No import route on earth captures a live <canvas>.

step_3_all_actions.text: AI outlines two distinct migration routes (Plugin vs. MCP).
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: Two routes to get pages → Figma

step_3_all_actions.text: AI suggests specific learning resources for the user.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: Watch these first (you decide by seeing)

step_3_all_actions.text: AI requests a decision from the user to proceed with a specific route.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: The decision I need from you

step_3_all_actions.text: User asks about the source for the editable Figma truth.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: What should the editable Figma source of truth be built from?

step_3_all_actions.text: User asks if the design-system audit should be done before Figma migration.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: Do you want the design-system AUDIT done first, before any Figma migration?

step_3_all_actions.text: AI describes the architected phased audit-first workflow.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: Architected phased audit-first workflow with code extraction and visual drift capture.

step_3_all_actions.text: AI explains the reasoning and context for the audit process.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: Before diving into Step 1 of the audit track, I need to lay out the reasoning and context

step_3_all_actions.text: AI outlines the plan for AntiGravity to scan the codebase and produce a drift inventory.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: So the plan is to have AntiGravity scan the codebase and produce a drift inventory

step_3_all_actions.text: AI states the need to confirm AntiGravity has the repository ready.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: Before kicking off that extraction, I need to confirm AntiGravity has the repo open and ready to scan.

step_3_all_actions.text: AI decides the scope of the audit to include all shipped pages.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: The scope question: should we audit all shipped pages or just the completed ones? I'll go with all shipped pages to be thorough.

step_3_all_actions.text: AI defines the audit method and what constitutes drift.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: we're treating colors_and_type.css as the canonical source, and anything not traceable to a token there counts as drift.

step_3_all_actions.text: AI clarifies the sequencing of tasks.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: I'm also clarifying the sequencing: after the preamble, I wait for "start task" and then deliver one complete step

step_3_all_actions.text: AI presents the final structure of the audit and migration tracks.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: Phase 9 — Design System Formalization + Figma Migration

step_3_all_actions.text: AI explains the purpose of Step 1.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: WHY: You can't audit drift without knowing what's actually applied across the pages

step_3_all_actions.text: AI defines the categories of drift for the audit.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: Three buckets: exact match (good), near-miss... and orphan

step_3_all_actions.text: AI requests confirmation on the audit scope and canonical reference.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: DECISIONS / REFERENCES — confirm or correct before we start

step_3_all_actions.text: AI invites the user to trigger the next step.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: Reply "start task" and I'll give you the full AntiGravity brief + testing checklist.

step_3_all_actions.text: User requests to start the task.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: start task

step_3_all_actions.text: AI reports that it has architected the design audit brief.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: Architected design audit brief with classification thresholds.

step_3_all_actions.text: AI describes the process of preparing the AntiGravity brief.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: Now I'm preparing the AntiGravity brief for him—he wants a detailed, outcome-focused prompt that scans his portfolio site repo and extracts key information

step_3_all_actions.text: AI explains its reasoning for the scope and structure of the audit brief.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: I'm thinking through the scope carefully — the agent will need to handle CSS files, inline styles in JSX, and hardcoded color values scattered through JavaScript and shader code

step_3_all_actions.text: AI instructs the user to confirm the repository path.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: confirm the repo path in the brief matches yours

step_3_all_actions.text: AI provides the AntiGravity brief for the user to paste.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: TASK: Audit design-token drift across the site. READ-ONLY. Do not modify any source file. Produce one report file.

step_3_all_actions.text: AI explains the rationale behind the audit methodology.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: The whole audit hinges on the near-miss bucket. An orphan (some random #777) is obvious and harmless to spot.

step_3_all_actions.text: AI provides a testing checklist for the user.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote:
✅ Testing checklist

design-audit-raw.md exists at repo root and opens cleanly.

step_3_all_actions.text: AI instructs the user on the next steps after the audit is complete.
step_3_all_actions.evidence_quote: When it's done, drop design-audit-raw.md into this chat and reply "Finish Step"
